summary: Backend (auth, buyers, settings, seed idempotency, session expiry, logout) all passing. Frontend sign-in, unauth redirect, editor/viewer role behaviour, nav routing, disabled/enabled primary actions, and role-badge all passing. One bug: sign-out lands on /sign-in instead of /signed-out.
passed: Startup seed: 5 buyers with correct schema (purchase_potential HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW, segment directory/discover, outreach_status NONE default, all required keys)
Seed idempotency: after backend restart, buyers count stays 5 and settings count stays 1
Editor Bearer token: /api/auth/me returns role='editor' for @qalara.com email
Viewer Bearer token: /api/auth/me returns role='viewer' for gmail.com email
Editor Bearer: GET /api/buyers returns 5 buyers list
Editor Bearer: GET /api/settings/qalara_profile returns object with expected keys
SignIn page renders with data-testid signin-page, brand-logo, google-signin-btn
Editor session cookie renders AppShell with sidebar navs (nav-dashboard/discover/outreach/impact/settings), topbar, role-badge='editor', user-name visible
Each nav click routes to correct Coming Soon page (coming-soon-dashboard/discover/outreach/impact/settings)
Editor: primary-action button enabled; disabled-primary-action not present
Viewer session: role-badge='viewer', 'Demo mode' pill visible, disabled-primary-action present, primary-action absent

failed.issue: Clicking sign-out lands on /sign-in instead of /signed-out. After logout() clears user, AppShell (protected wrapper) renders <Navigate to='/sign-in' replace /> which pre-empts the navigate('/signed-out') call in TopBar.handleSignOut. The /signed-out page and its return-signin-link data-testid are correctly implemented but unreachable via the UI.
failed.evidence: Playwright: after clicking user-menu-trigger -> sign-out-btn, page.url resolves to https://<host>/sign-in; data-testid='signed-out-page' never appears (timeout 10s). Reproduced twice.

action_items: In TopBar.handleSignOut, navigate to '/signed-out' BEFORE calling logout(); OR mark /signed-out as a public route accessible even when user is null (already is a top-level route) and change AppShell to redirect to '/signed-out' when user becomes null due to explicit logout (e.g., set a 'justLoggedOut' flag in AuthContext, or navigate first then clear user). Simplest fix: in AuthContext.logout, after API call, call navigate('/signed-out') before setUser(null), or setUser(null) then use a useEffect in AppShell that checks a logout flag.
